title: Microsoft Copilot data protection: Zscaler Copilot Security for Microsoft

prose.text: {{cdp-onedrive}} {{cdp-paths}} Which capability uses which path is open {{gap:cdp-api-inline}}.
{{cdp-risk}} {{cdp-platform}} The DSPM and CASB subjects are [[dspm.overview]] and [[portfolio.casb]].

Whether the deployment guide is captured is open {{gap:cdp-guide}}. Whether Copilot indexes SharePoint and Teams data too is open {{gap:cdp-sources}}. Whether the product has its own SDK is open {{gap:cdp-sdk}}.

checks.do: Before stating a Copilot deployment step, check whether the deployment guide is captured; if it is not, say the step is open.
For a question about which Copilot data sources are covered, answer with OneDrive only and name the SharePoint and Teams question as open.

cdp-marketed.statement: The page is titled Zscaler Copilot Security for Microsoft, and its headline is Control Data Security and Oversharing in Microsoft Copilot.

quotes: Control Data Security and Oversharing in Microsoft Copilot

cdp-four.statement: The page lists four security functions: prompt visibility and DLP, permission remediation, data classification and configuration hardening.

quotes: Full visibility into Copilot user prompts; block sensitive data inputs with DLP
Prevent Copilot oversharing by removing excessive sharing permissions
Add missing Purview sensitivity labels to restrict Copilot access
Identify and close dangerous misconfigurations in Microsoft 365 and Copilot settings

cdp-onedrive.statement: The OneDrive item says the product fixes improperly permissioned data that Copilot can overconsume and share.

quotes: fixes improperly permissioned data that Copilot can overconsume and share

cdp-paths.statement: The page says the product uses both API and inline security paths to control Copilot deployments.

quotes: Uses both **API and inline** security paths to enable robust control over Copilot deployments

cdp-risk.statement: The page says that without DLP, classification and permission discipline, oversharing risk compounds, because the data Copilot indexes flows back to users via prompts.

quotes: without DLP / classification / permission discipline, oversharing risk compounds
the same data Copilot indexes flows back to users via prompts

cdp-platform.statement: The product is part of Zscaler's Data Security pillar within the unified Zero Trust platform, and complements existing DLP, CASB and DSPM solutions.

quotes: Part of Zscaler's Data Security pillar within the unified Zero Trust platform.
Complements existing DLP, CASB, and DSPM solutions for comprehensive data protection.

cdp-guide.title: Whether the Copilot deployment guide is captured and canonical
cdp-guide.detail: Unverified legacy statement: 'Vendored deployment guide is the canonical operational reference.' The capture names Zscaler-Microsoft-Copilot-Deployment-Guide-FINAL.pdf under vendor/zscaler-help/downloads/, but that file is not in the repository and no capture of it exists.

cdp-sources.title: Which Microsoft data sources Copilot indexes
cdp-sources.detail: Unverified legacy statement: 'Copilot indexes data from OneDrive / SharePoint / Teams and can surface it to underprivileged users via prompts.' The capture names OneDrive only.

cdp-api-inline.title: Which Copilot capability uses the API path and which the inline path
cdp-api-inline.detail: Unverified legacy statement: 'API-based (data classification, permissions) and inline (prompt DLP) integration paths.' The capture says both paths exist and does not map capabilities to them.

cdp-sdk.title: Whether the Copilot product has its own SDK surface
cdp-sdk.detail: Unverified legacy statement: 'No SDK surface specific to this product.' The vendored SDK code mentions Copilot only as a cloud-app category value, not as a product surface, but no captured page states the product has or lacks an API.
